issues.description: The problem UML and textual description list checkOrderReady() as a void method (UML: +checkOrderReady(): void), but the solution implements it as public boolean checkOrderReady(). This mismatch can confuse students about the required signature (whether to return a boolean) and may lead to inconsistent implementations.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method return type consistent across materials. Either update the problem statement/UML to allow a boolean return (and explain its meaning) or change the solution to implement checkOrderReady() as void (removing the boolean return). Preferably align with the UML/text by using void and rely on side-effects/printing for readiness.

issues.description: There is an inconsistency between the UML and the textual requirements about which members should be static. The UML lists calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int without indicating it is static, while the textual instructions explicitly require the stock attribute and the calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery methods to be static. This discrepancy (UML vs. textual note) could confuse students which declaration to follow.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify and align the UML and textual description: update the UML to indicate that stock is a static (and final) attribute and mark calculateTotalPrice and acceptSupplyDelivery as static methods, or add a note in the UML commenting on their static nature. Ensuring both UML and text consistently declare these members as static will prevent confusion.
